correctness.rationale: The resultant is the norm of c-vα for α²=-v, namely c²+v³; a zero would make -v a square. For e=χ(-1), expand the nonzero-v mask (1-eχ(v))/2 and invert v in the weighted sum to get 2D=H-e(K-1)-1. If cubing permutes the field, H=K=0 and only q=3 can give |D|=(q-1)/2. Otherwise the cube-root multiplicity 1+ψ+ψ̄, with the order-three character zero at zero, gives H=wJ+w̄J̄ and K=w̄J+wJ̄ for w=ψ(c²). The Gauss/Jacobi quotient gives |J|=√q. For q≡1 (mod 12) cubes give D=0 and noncubes require q≤7+4√3, leaving 13. For q≡7 (mod 12) the cube bound is 2√q+1 and the noncube bound is √q+1, leaving 7 and 19 for cubes and 7 for noncubes. These ranges exhaust odd prime powers, including characteristic three. Direct prime-field arithmetic at c=1,2,4 gives (3,-3,-3), (0,6,-6), (-9,3,3) for q=7,13,19; these are representatives of the three cube classes in each case. All signs are nonzero, so a nonunanimous signature must contain both signs. value.rationale: Trace-zero irreducibles are a canonical test family in odd characteristic, and square-class unanimity is exactly failure of that entire family to distinguish the two nonzero classes. A sharp cutoff and complete exceptional cube classes settle that failure uniformly, including a last exception at 19 not apparent from the individual classical sum identities. The value is the extremal classification, not the one-test case at q=3 or a bounded residue table.
